rv.q: But otherwise this is a sensational vision of ultrasonic mayhem.
Factor in a sharp script that drips with merciless satire, and what you have is the most daring and original show to arrive in the West End in recent memory.
His is a perfectly timed, lethally funny satirical sting operation.

Rigby, who has the unparalleled quality of being annoying in the most endearing way, doesn't just perform Basden's exquisite script: he blows every single line up, making each one a balloon or a bomb depending how mad he's feeling.
Daniel Rigby's performance as The Maniac, the mischief maker who uncovers brazen police malpractice, is nothing short of mesmerising.
Tom Basden’s adaptation of Accidental Death of an Anarchist is an astonishing assault on the senses.
Seeing it in its latest incarnation, however, I felt that, for all the ingenuity of Raggett, Basden and Rigby, there was slightly too much sugar and not quite enough pill.
If you see one play in the West End this summer, make it this one.
The result is an unapologetic attack on those institutions fundamentally charged with upholding the rule of law and by inference, the moral fabric of decent, law-abiding society.
But in both cases, I couldn’t help tuning out after a while, temperamentally attuned to the material in both cases though I am.
Accidental Death of an Anarchist is an absolute riot – a belly-aching tour-de-force that wraps some sobering truths in masterful comedy.
Accidental Death of an Anarchist has its audience howling for about ninety percent of the running time; sometimes resulting in us missing the next joke because the laughter was so loud.
This is a jarring, suddenly dark production which leaves you travelling from bursts of laughter to solemn, thought-provoking moments of the real outside world.
It’s a damning attack on the Metropolitan Police, and exposes the corruption, incompetence and prejudice of the institution.
Rigby commands the role perfectly, bringing the slapstick, silly and unexpected aspects of this character out whilst also remaining charming for the audience.
Overall, it is a very funny farce that has sharp teeth.

cn.t: Critics celebrate this high-octane adaptation as urgently timely and hilariously sharp, with Daniel Rigby's astonishing performance and Tom Basden's merciless script delivering a relentless barrage of satire that brilliantly skewers police corruption.
